newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin Ukraine trip most crucial in 1997 -Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin Ukraine trip most crucial in 1997 -Kremlin.

text.p: The Kremlin said on Friday that Russian President Boris Yeltsin's trip to Ukraine later in the day would be his most testing and crucial foreign policy step this year, Interfax news agency said.
"(It is) the most difficult visit and the most important foreign policy act by the Russian President in 1997," the agency quoted Yeltsin's spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying.

Yastrzhembsky said that Yeltsin saw his trip to Kiev as even more important than a Russia-NATO summit in Paris this week at which the former Cold War foes signed a deal outlining a new cooperative relationship.
"The closer the ties between Russia and Ukraine, the fewer the headaches in its (Russia's) relations with NATO," Interfax quoted the Kremlin spokesman as saying.

Yeltsin is due to arrive in Kiev on Friday afternoon on a visit postponed over and over again due to tensions between Russia and its southern neighbour. On Saturday, he is expected to sign a long-awaited friendship and cooperation treaty with Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma.

"The documents which are expected to be signed in Kiev, will become a true breakthrough in Russia's bilateral relations with Ukraine. On their basis one can resolve practically all negative problems which have appeared in recent years in relations between the two countries," Yastrzhembsky said.
